scope.q: What is the acceptable latency and accuracy for part lookup, considering technicians are often on-site in potentially low-connectivity areas?
scope.why: This determines the technical approach for data processing (e.g., local vs. cloud inference) and the robustness required for the solution.

scope.q: Are there existing digital systems that catalog units and parts, even if not linked, or is the entire source of truth within these scanned PDFs?
scope.why: Understanding existing data sources helps determine if we need to build a knowledge graph from scratch or integrate with partial existing structured data.

scope.q: What is the expected volume of daily queries, and how many unique parts and units are covered across the thousands of PDFs?
scope.why: This impacts the scalability requirements for the backend processing and retrieval systems, as well as the scope of data ingestion.

decomposition.title: Document Ingestion & OCR
decomposition.why: This foundational step converts unstructured image-based PDFs into searchable text and extracts initial metadata.

decomposition.title: Information Extraction & Knowledge Graph Construction
decomposition.why: This involves identifying entities (parts, units) and relationships from the extracted text to build a structured, queryable knowledge base.

decomposition.title: Search & Retrieval Engine
decomposition.why: This component enables efficient querying against the knowledge graph to find relevant parts for specific units or vice-versa.

decomposition.title: User Interface & Interaction Layer
decomposition.why: This provides a simple, intuitive way for field technicians to submit queries and receive answers on their devices.

decomposition.title: Feedback & Improvement Loop
decomposition.why: This is crucial for capturing user feedback and system performance to continuously refine extraction models and search accuracy.

sprint.title: Set up Ingestion Pipeline & Basic OCR
sprint.deliv: A functional script that can OCR a sample PDF and output raw text.

sprint.title: Develop Entity Extraction Models
sprint.deliv: A trained model that can identify 'part numbers' and 'unit models' from OCR'd text with reasonable accuracy on a test set.

sprint.title: Implement Knowledge Graph Schema & Ingestion
sprint.deliv: A defined knowledge graph schema and a script that ingests extracted entities and relationships from sample data into a graph database.

sprint.title: Build Core Search API
sprint.deliv: A REST API endpoint that takes a 'unit model' and returns associated 'part numbers' from the knowledge graph.

sprint.title: Prototype Technician UI (Mobile Web)
sprint.deliv: A basic web-based UI accessible on mobile that can submit a query to the API and display the results.

sprint.title: Initial Data Load & Testing
sprint.deliv: 200-500 PDFs processed end-to-end, with a functional UI for querying their contents and basic accuracy validation.

sprint.title: Feedback Mechanism & Refinement
sprint.deliv: A button in the UI to mark an answer as 'helpful' or 'unhelpful', logging feedback for future model retraining.

risks.risk: Poor OCR quality on older, low-resolution scanned manuals leads to inaccurate text extraction and poor downstream results.
risks.mitigation: Implement pre-processing steps (e.g., de-skewing, noise reduction) and use multiple OCR engines to compare results, falling back to human review for critical pages.

risks.risk: Inconsistent terminology and formatting across thousands of diverse manuals makes entity and relationship extraction difficult and error-prone.
risks.mitigation: Develop robust, adaptable NLP models using few-shot learning or rule-based systems for common patterns, and implement a human-in-the-loop validation process for high-confidence extractions.

risks.risk: Scalability issues with processing thousands of PDFs and building a large knowledge graph within acceptable timeframes.
risks.mitigation: Utilize distributed processing frameworks (e.g., Spark) for OCR and extraction, and optimize graph database indexing strategies for efficient storage and querying.

risks.risk: Field technicians struggle with a new interface or receive irrelevant results, leading to low adoption and continued calls to the depot.
risks.mitigation: Conduct early user testing with a small group of technicians to gather feedback on UI/UX and search relevance, iterating quickly on design and model improvements.
